critique.problems: 首屏主要显示日期和四个价格列，涨跌幅被截在视口边缘；成交指标需要向右滚动较远才能看到。
critique.cause: 日期列108px、四个价格列各59px，合计已占344px；成交量113px和成交额129px让两个长表头保持单行，但将总宽度推至662px。

critique.good: 保留完整日期和数值，四个价格列仍等宽；成交表头换行后，横向滚动距离比r0A减少53px。
critique.problems: 首屏仍只露出涨跌幅的一部分，成交指标需要滚动查看；两个成交表头换行使表头行明显高于数据行。
critique.cause: 日期及价格列仍合计344px；成交量90px和成交额99px足以容纳最长不可拆内容，但不足以容纳各自的单行表头。

critique.good: 整张表处于视口内，无需横向滚动。
critique.problems: 日期、价格、百分比和成交数字被拆成多行，难以识别和比较；表头竖向堆叠，行高过大，同一交易日的数据也不易作为一个整体阅读。
critique.cause: 日期列仅52px，价格列各40px，涨跌幅45px，成交列49px和53px；扣除21px内边距及边框后，所有这些列都不足以容纳对应的最长不可拆内容。

critique.good: 日期和四个价格均保持完整；四个价格列等宽，便于横向和纵向比较。成交量表头保持一行，所有数据均无词中拆分。
critique.problems: 初始视口刚好容纳日期和四个价格列，却只露出涨跌幅的一小部分；成交指标需要横向滚动。成交额表头换行后拉高了整行表头。
critique.cause: 日期列108px、四个价格列各59px，合计344px，留给涨跌幅的视口空间很少。成交额列99px可容纳最长的不可拆分内容，但不足以容纳108px的整行表头及内边距。

critique.good: 日期、价格和所有数值保持完整，四个价格列的节奏一致。成交额表头保持一行。
critique.problems: 初始视口同样只露出涨跌幅的一小部分，两个成交指标都需要滚动查看。成交量表头换行仍使表头行升高，因此成交额表头保持一行并未降低整行高度。
critique.cause: 前六列宽度与r1A相同。成交量列90px不足以容纳整行表头；成交额列129px足以容纳整行表头，但比保持其内容不拆分所需的99px多30px。

critique.good: 日期和四列价格保持完整，价格列等宽，便于横向比较；成交量与成交额表头换行，节省横向空间。
critique.problems: 首次视野只容纳日期和四列价格，涨跌幅及成交数据需要横向滚动；表头比数据行高，增加了纵向留白。
critique.cause: 日期108px与四个59px价格列合计344px，几乎占满视口；成交量90px、成交额99px不足以让各自表头单行显示。

critique.good: 所有表头与数据均保持单行，行高一致，四列价格的节奏清晰，整张表更紧凑。
critique.problems: 首次视野与r2A基本相同，但查看右侧成交数据需要滚动更远；两个成交列表头单行所带来的横向空间成本较高。
critique.cause: 成交量113px、成交额129px分别容纳了完整表头，使总宽度比r2A增加53px。

r0A.idea: 总宽661px，所有内容保持单行，四个价格列等宽，便于比较，但读者需要横向滚动查看后面的指标。

r0B.idea: 总宽608px，保持日期和数值完整，让两个成交指标的表头换行，以增加表头高度换取较少的横向滚动。

r0C.idea: 总宽359px，全部列首次可见且四个价格列等宽，但日期、价格和其他数值都会被迫拆行，适合优先要求无需横向滚动的场景。

r1A.idea: 以r0B为基础，将成交量列加宽至113px，使其表头保持单行；成交额仍在指标与单位之间换行。总宽632px，在表头清晰度与滚动距离之间尝试折中。

r1B.idea: 保留r0B的紧凑成交量列，将成交额列加宽至129px，使较长的成交额表头保持单行。总宽639px，可比较两种表头换行位置的视觉效果。

r2A.idea: 保留日期、价格和数值的完整性，让两个成交指标表头换行。总宽608px，比r1A少24px、比r1B少31px，减少查看末列所需的滚动；初始视口中的列分布不变。

r2B.idea: 将两个成交指标列都加宽至可容纳单行表头，尝试降低表头高度并保持单位与指标名称同行。代价是总宽661px，需要更多横向滚动。

r3A.idea: 将日期列由108px缩至64px，让日期在连字符处换行，保留四列价格的等宽节奏及数值完整性；沿用较窄的成交列。总宽降至565px，首次视野可露出更多涨跌幅，但日期换行会增加数据行高度，需要结合渲染结果判断查找日期是否仍然顺畅。

understanding.purpose: 按日期展示行情，供读者比较每日价格、涨跌幅和成交情况。
understanding.reading: 读者先沿日期纵向查找交易日，再横向比较同一日的开盘、最高、最低和收盘价，并查看涨跌幅及成交情况；也可纵向比较同一指标的变化。
groups: 开盘、最高、最低、收盘：四个同类价格指标，适合保持相同宽度和稳定节奏。
涨跌幅：与价格相关的变化指标，符号和百分号共同表达方向与幅度。
成交量（手）、成交额（万元）：分别表示交易数量和金额，表头中的单位帮助正确解读数值。
keep_intact: 日期应尽量作为完整的交易日标识。
价格、带正负号的百分比和成交数值应尽量保持完整，避免小数点、符号或数字被拆到另一行。
may_wrap: 成交量和成交额表头可在指标名称与括号内单位之间自然换行。
若日期或数值被迫拆行，现有行高不能可靠地吸收换行，整行会随最高单元格增高。

bad.why: Dates, prices, percentages and transaction figures break across multiple lines, making values difficult to recognize and compare. The tall, narrow headers also overwhelm the data.
Every date breaks across three lines, making the row labels harder to scan and more than doubling the body row height. The table still requires substantial horizontal scrolling.

final.rationale: r0B and r2A are identical: they preserve complete dates and numeric values while keeping the four price columns equal in width. The two longer transaction headers wrap, but the data rows remain compact and aligned. This saves 53px of horizontal travel compared with the fully unwrapped r0A and r2B, while the initial viewport still shows the date and all four prices.

general: Keep values intact when splitting them would impede recognition or comparison.
Give columns with the same role a consistent rhythm, and allow longer headers to wrap when their data remains easy to scan.
Judge horizontal scrolling against the legibility gained and the relationships visible in the initial viewport.
specific: The four price columns have identical content-width requirements and benefit from matching widths.
The date needs substantially more width than a price to remain on one line; narrowing it still does not eliminate scrolling.
Both transaction headers can wrap without increasing the height of the data rows.

final.tradeoffs: The preferred layout reduces scrolling at the cost of a taller header. r0A and r2B keep every header on one line, which some readers may find cleaner, but require more horizontal travel.
final.uncertain: The ranges are conservative design estimates, not tested breakpoints; widths near their limits should be rendered to confirm that values remain intact. A designer could reasonably prefer the fully unwrapped headers if horizontal scrolling is a minor concern.

A.why: Nearly every value is broken across lines, including dates, prices and percentages. The tall, fragmented rows make comparison difficult.

B.why: Prices and percentages remain readable at first sight, but dates split across three lines, weakening the row rhythm. The remaining columns require scrolling.

C.why: Dates and the four price columns stay intact in a compact, easy-to-scan grid. The percentage column starts at the viewport edge, so the reader must scroll to see it and the later columns.

D.why: The visible dates and prices remain intact and align clearly, though the tall header adds white space. Later columns require horizontal scrolling.

E.why: The visible dates and prices are intact and easy to compare, though the tall header adds white space. Later columns require horizontal scrolling.

F.why: Prices, dates and larger numbers split into fragments, making both row reading and column comparison difficult despite fitting within the viewport.

reviews.unsure: The supplied view shows only the left portion of B, C, D and E, so I cannot assess the widths and wrapping of their later columns or the full scrolling cost. C has the most compact header among the visible alternatives.

A.why: Dates and the four price columns remain intact and easy to compare. The percentage and trading columns require horizontal scrolling.

B.why: Nearly every date and number breaks across several lines, and the stacked headers make the columns difficult to scan.

C.why: The visible dates and prices stay intact in compact, readable rows. The remaining columns require horizontal scrolling.

D.why: The visible dates and prices remain intact and align clearly for comparison. The remaining columns require horizontal scrolling.

E.why: Prices and percentages stay intact, but every date breaks across three lines, making the row labels harder to read; the trading columns still require scrolling.

F.why: Dates, prices and trading figures fragment across lines, while tall stacked headers and rows make comparisons difficult.

reviews.unsure: A, C and D look effectively identical in the supplied visible portions. Their offscreen columns cannot be assessed, so their relative quality is uncertain.
